predecessors.name: Gojoseon (Old Joseon)
predecessors.text: Xuantu's first seat, 'Fort Okjeo': the page says only 'the northern Korean Peninsula'; the Lintun page quotes Bowman that 'Lintun and originally Xuantu were centered on the east coast of northern…

successors.name: Goguryeo
successors.text: the 'new Xuantu, which had retreated west to present-day Fushun', four counties

ledger.x: 107 BCE: the Han found Xuantu after the conquest of Wiman Joseon.
82 BCE: Lintun is merged into Xuantu.
75 BCE: Xuantu's seat leaves Fort Okjeo.
75 BCE: the Lintun remnant goes to Lelang.
75 BCE: the Korean coast is left behind.
75 BCE: Xuantu is rebuilt around Gaogouli County in the Tonghua region; the page names three counties (Gaogouli, Shangyintai, Xigaima) and no land.
204: Xuantu falls under the Gongsun of Liaodong.
238: Wei conquers Xuantu with the Gongsun.
319: the last Han commandery in Manchuria ends.

wars.name: Buyeo attacks on Xuantu
wars.outcome: Buyeo is an Eastern Han ally: 'c.

wars.name: Goguryeo-Wei War
wars.outcome: Cao Wei victory: Guanqiu Jian 'set out from Xuantu Commandery into Goguryeo with seven legions' and Wang Qi, grand administrator of Xuantu, pursued King Dongcheon into the Okjeo lands.

certainty.note: The pages give counties and seats but no boundaries; the first location is disputed (peninsula or Shenyang), and the post-75 BCE seat is 'most probably' Tonghua.
